claims.statement: THE AFFORDANCE IS NEVER A DEAD BUTTON: the WHAT'S NEXT card carries Drive, and every state where it cannot run is surfaced beside it in the same terms the approve uses — a boundary derivation (advance-leg/closure-needed/none: 'the move here is yours, not the machine's'), a dirty tree with its NAMED blocker count, an integrity snapshot still in flight, or no frontmost-ready task. driveEnablement is a pure function of the card's own derivation, the lazy integrity verdict and executable — the page never guesses a verdict the write would refuse, and a NON-200 refusal (drive-busy on the shared single-flight slot, provider-config) renders the server's own code and message, uninvented. Pinned by 6 DOM tests, incl. two booted identically that differ ONLY in the integrity read (landed -> enabled, in flight -> disabled) and a mid-run provider-failure stop with zero executed calls.

THE OUTCOME IS RENDERED, NOT SUMMARIZED: the stop and its route reason, every call that EXECUTED (each accepted, with what it wrote), the call REFUSED BY NAME with its code and reason, and — at the authored-work boundary — the DRAFTED contract marked GENERATED with its provenance (model - provider - turn - run - at), its kind/id, groundedOn, rationale and its bytes. RECORDED DECISION: the draft POINTS AT THE COMMAND (ann spawn! <id> '<contract>') instead of offering a spawn button — spawn! is deliberately not a route on this service (the named scope boundary) and a button would make the page a command runner to save a copy-paste. The decision is recorded in renderDraft's docblock and in the commit message, and the test enforces it: the draft box renders ZERO buttons and ZERO links, and says 'the machine never spawns'.

THE COST AND THE CREDENTIAL ARE ON THE PAGE BEFORE THE CLICK: a DRIVE runs the engine's own LLM loop — REAL provider calls, billed to the SERVER-SIDE key, which never reaches this page; one operate-loop action at a time (the slot is shared with Approve); a provider failure stops the run with ZERO writes. The notice is served markup the script never touches, so the assertion is on the bytes the server sends. The provider failure itself is shown as the fact it is (stop provider-failure, error-styled, no call made), and the existing credential e2e already proves a configured key appears in no response body.

PROVEN WITH A STUB PROVIDER, NO LIVE CALLS: 4 e2e cases over real HTTP. (1) the drive-busy 409 — the overlap is a FIXTURE, not a sleep: the stub brakes its reply and the second request is fired only after the provider RECEIVED the first, so the route's synchronous claim is provably held; the refused drive never reaches the provider (one completion for two requests) and the brake is reset and its holder awaited so no slot leaks across tests. (2) the page's own flow over real HTTP — GET / carries the affordance's ids, the card enables it, POST /api/drive {} runs, and the re-read reports the journey the drive moved. (3) the boundary/blocker states — the integrity verdict names the exact tracked file it found, restored afterwards. (4) the boundary draft writes NOTHING: every node's raw event bytes are compared before and after, so a node that APPEARED fails too, and the derivation still stands at the boundary. Vanilla UI, no new dependency.

ALL FOUR CHECKS CAPTURED AT THIS COMMIT: npm test PASS (46 files, 908 tests — 893 baseline + 11 DOM + 4 e2e), npm run typecheck PASS (tsc --noEmit), ann check PASS (no gate gaps), ann verify PASS (clean, 0 drifts). The suite count is a real gate: the pretest tsc step caught a missing FakeEl.disabled that vitest's esbuild transform had let through, so npm test aborts on a type error rather than reporting green. Committed 1f5e213 with the recorded AC-2 decision in the message; reads and tests only — no new event, status, write path or dependency.
